parent.indexbuild2: The round-2 producer differs from the row's in two computations, neither of which changes a value. (C9) State loop: for a regular state (l != r, l != 0, r != 0; exactly the states whose parent denominator a*ps is non-zero, since squaring is injective and GF(2^83) has no zero divisors) the parent computes a = (l+r)^2, p = l r, ps = p^2, c = ps + b, inv = (a ps)^-1, q = p (ps inv) = p/a and d = (c a)(a inv) = c a/ps. The round-2 loop computes q = p ((l+r)^-1)^2 and d = c (l^-1 + r^-1)^2, the same field elements because a/ps = ((l+r)/(l r))^2 = (1/l + 1/r)^2. Every inverse is a field inverse (1/l and 1/r: the inverse of a representative squared k times is the inverse of its k-th Frobenius shift, each checked by a product at build time; 1/(l+r): Montgomery's trick over four interleaved chains, the inverse of a non-zero element being unique), and field elements have one reduced representation, so q and d are bit for bit the parent's; the trace test, the half trace, the root order and the to_normal images then are the parent's. An irregular state takes s3_x_roots_128(gf, b, l, r), which is what the parent's finish returns for a zero denominator. States are pushed in the parent's (left, right, relative) order, so stored_states_blake3 is the parent's. (C7) Insert loop: for a nonconstant 83-bit word v, z_1 = !v and z_(j+1) = z_j & rotl(z_j, 1) has bit p set iff bits p..p-j are zero (cyclically), so the last nonzero z_j is Z_L (L the longest zero run), the tops of all longest zero runs, which is the run set lift_scan's greedy lifting ends with (lift2/src/lib.rs). The candidate rotations s = N-1-p and the choice (least rotation, ties to the smaller shift, an order-independent minimum) are lift_scan's, and 0 and the all-ones word return shift 0 as in lift_scan; so the key and shift equal lift_scan's for every word. In the eight-lane form a lane that reaches its Z_L keeps it by a select while the other lanes continue; the word 0 starts at z = 0. Keys are computed once per root in increasing root order (eight at a time, the tail one at a time by the parent's call), the planted counter is incremented once per root in lift_plant, the prefetch is a hint, and insert_if_absent receives the parent's (key, value) sequence, so every slot word, and table_slots_blake3, is the parent's. Relations, probes, the rank stage and the online scan read only the index and the self-test verdict, so they are the parent's. Checked locally on every stored root of K600, M38 and M10 (inputs/local_exactness.json) and gated per process and per base in the run.

parent.indexbuild: The derived producer differs from the row's in three computations, none of which changes a value. (1) State loop: S3Solver128::roots computes prepare, one inversion of the denominator a*ps (zero takes the scalar fallback) and finish. RootBatch128::solve computes the same prepare, inverts the product of the row's non-zero denominators once and recovers each inverse as (prefix product) x (inverse of the running product), which is that denominator's field inverse because inverses in GF(2^83) are unique; finish then returns the same two roots in the same order. States are pushed in the parent's (left, right, relative) order, so stored_states_blake3 is the parent's. (2) Insert loop: index_canonical128 is a pure function of the root (plus the planted counter, called once per root in the same order), so computing it 32 roots early changes no key or shift; the prefetch is a hint without architectural effect; insert_if_absent is called with the same (key, value) sequence into the same table, so every slot word, and table_slots_blake3, is the parent's. (3) Self-test: the parent returns false iff some image of [0, domain) is >= domain or an in-range image repeats, else visited == len; the lanes loop evaluates the same apply on the same indices and the same checks on the images in index order, eight applies ahead of their checks, so it returns the same boolean. Relations, probes, the rank stage and the online scan read only the index and the self-test verdict, so they are the parent's. Gated per process and per base on K600, M38 and M10.
parent.parent: Frobenius phi acts on the prime-order subgroup as multiplication by lambda (lambda^2 - lambda + 2 = 0 mod r), so for alpha = a + b tau, alpha(R) = [a]R + [b]phi(R) = [(a + b lambda) mod r]R, and every member +-phi^k(alpha(R_c)) of orbit (c, alpha) has discrete log +-(a + b lambda) lambda^k log R_c. The header carries exactly these labels; verify_closure.py re-derives every member and label from the orbit representative and checks each representative against [w]R_c and, with the table, against [w L_c]G, in the pinned oracle. A relation found by the unchanged S3 search is checked in the group by the unchanged lift (four base points summing to the attempt's point), so its row sum_i coeff_i L_{c_i} = a (+ L_c for the guided column) holds exactly; full rank gives the unique logs, checked [L_c]G = R_c in process and equal to B's archived logs of the same R_c. A target's scalar is checked [d]G = Q in process and replayed in the oracle, and must equal the baseline's and the tuned rho's. The root index, probe loop and scan are the rank-probe producer's code, built from the closure's orbit representatives. With KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift the index build keys every stored state's two normal-basis roots with lift_scan instead of the selected canonicalizer; both return the least rotation of the 83-bit word and the least shift reaching it, the stored states are computed before and independently of that call, so the table receives the same inserts in the same order and its slot array is the same word for word (index-lift's argument). The layout digests gate this per process on every base, so every relation, probe count, rank table and scalar of a lift-built index is the selected-built index's.

exactness_argument.rankfinder: The rank-finder producer differs from the row's in one computation, which does not change a value. In scan_state128_frame (KIC_RANK_SOLVE=frame and frame_plant, used only by the rank stage) the parent computes every partner word's key as target_canonical::<CANON_LIFT>, i.e. lift_scan_wide(v, 83), right after the word. The derived loop pushes the same partner words in the same order with the same candidate index and pair starts, and whenever eight keys are pending computes their (canonical, shift) with lift_linear_lanes8::<83>, the parent's own C7 function, whose result equals lift_scan's for every 83-bit word: for a nonconstant word v, z_1 = !v and z_(j+1) = z_j & rotl(z_j, 1) has bit p set iff bits p..p-j are zero (cyclically), so the last nonzero z_j is Z_L, the tops of all longest zero runs, lift_scan's final run set; the candidate rotations and the order-independent choice (least rotation, ties to the smaller shift) are lift_scan's; 0 and the all-ones word give shift 0. The at most seven keys left at the end of a state take the parent's call. Every key is complete before the first lookup, the prefetch is a hint, and the probe loop is the parent's text, so probe positions, the first hit, the relation, root calls and every counter are the parent's. For any other canonicalizer or field size the parent's code runs. Checked by the crate tests against the parent's loop kept verbatim, and locally per seed on M38, M10 and K600 (inputs/local_exactness.json); gated per seed in the run.
